title: Lesson 1.3 Knowledge Check
description: Five questions on evaluating and fixing AI-generated cues. Unlimited attempts; your best score counts.

questions.text: What is the purpose of writing a cue sheet before generating any music?
options: To satisfy the tool's terms of service
To turn a vague request into a brief you can generate from and evaluate against
To reduce the number of credits used
questions.feedback: The cue sheet is both the prompt source and the evaluation standard.

questions.text: A generated cue has the right mood and instrumentation but keeps adding a sung vocal line. Which fix should you try first?
options: Edit the audio to remove the vocal
Switch to instrumental mode or a mood-based tool
questions.feedback: Persistent vocals are a mode or tool limitation, so change the mode or tool. Editing a vocal out of a mixed track is far harder.

questions.text: "I like it" is a sufficient evaluation of an AI-generated cue.
questions.feedback: Evaluation compares the output with the brief on named criteria such as mood match, tempo, instrumentation, structure, technical quality, and fit under dialogue.

questions.text: Which are among the six cue evaluation criteria used in this lesson? Select all that apply.
questions.feedback: The six criteria are mood match, tempo and energy, instrumentation, structure, technical quality, and fit under dialogue.

options: Using music that deliberately contrasts with the apparent emotion of the action
Using the same cue for every scene
Choosing a cue faster than the action
questions.feedback: Playing against the scene is a deliberate contrast that adds a layer of meaning.
